pr_title: fix(forms): ensure the field value of a FormGroup/FormArray always co…
pr_body:
…ntains enabled controls values

Prior to this change, the field value of a FormGroup or FormArray may contains disabled controls value.

PR close #35184

## PR Checklist

- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->
If you have a form which contains enabled controls, the value field contains the value of the enabled controls even if you add disabled controls of if you disable the form. The field value will always contain only enabled controls value.

The problem is : **Sometimes the field value doesn't contain only enabled controls value**
If you have a form disabled (either because it is disabled directly itself, or because all of its contained controls are disabled), the value field contains the value of the disabled controls until we add an enabled control or until we enable the form. When you add an enabled control or enable the form, the value field will always contain the value of the enabled controls even if you add disabled controls after.

Again, If you disable your form and you use setValue or patchValue method, the field value will contains the value you gave to theses methods, while the status of the form is disabled.
The field "value" sometimes doesn't contain only enabled controls value.
Issue Number: #35184


## What is the new behavior?
Now, the value field contains only enabled controls value.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

pr_comments: @TidianeRol, thanks for creating this PR. Existing Forms logic works as expected: the list of children may contain both enabled and disabled controls. Changing this behavior will result in a breaking change that would affect lots of use-cases. We'll revisit this question while working on Forms improvements/refactoring for future versions. I'll close this ticket for now to remove it from review queue. Thank you.

issue_context.title: When all the children form controls are disabled, the parent becomes disabled
comments:
@Mewster don't know why but can't visualize your code with this link https://angular-yiry8u.stackblitz.io, because the page stayed blank.
Can you show your code here or provide another way to visualize please?
@Tidiane0843 Sorry, I didn't understand how stackblitz works. Here is the correct link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-136pgu

> if you want to disable specific `formControl` without propagation you need to set `onlySelf` to `true`

That doesn't work too. Adding example to the stackblitz

"onlySelf" works only for the ancestors, not the parents anyway.

@Mewster I think the problem is the behavior of the field value. Because if you have a form which contains only disabled controls, the form should also be disabled. 
But the field value should only contain the enabled controls value while the getrawvalue contains all value (enabled or not). 
I fixed the behavior of the field value.
Hope it'll help

@TidianeRol I don't think that a form that contains only disabled controls should be disabled; in case the parent form has a validator, it should still be able to validate (even a simple Validators.required wouldn't work this way).
In my case I had a formarray that must contain (through a size validator) at least a specific number of children, that don't have to be valid in that specific moment and therefore disabled. But if they were all disabled, the children count validator wouldn't work.

I'm facing the same problem here, with a FormArray with disabled controls/children I want it's validation.required to keep working, but since it get's disabled two, required is ignored, I agree that disabling the parent, should disable it's children, but why the other way around?
Also ou could get your FormArray disabled by removing all enabled elements (using removeAt) with no clean way from preventing the user from doing so.
IMO, This behavior is wrong and should be changed.

WORKAROUND: since I know my Form Array could get disabled and it's required validator get ignored, I added another Validor in it's container, saying that value should be present:
```
  editForm = this.fb.group({
    id: [],
    ...
    items: this.fb.array([], [Validators.required])
  }, { validators: [c => c.value.items ? null : {itemsRequired: true}]});
```

Hi @Mewster, thanks for reporting the issue and providing a repro. It looks like the current logic works as expected. If your use-case require having a Form in a valid (i.e. not disabled) state, you can do that by using `FormGroup.enable()` API. I've created a copy of your repro and added an "Enable Form" button to illustrate that ([see here](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-136pgu-paezsg?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts)). Thank you.
Having to re-enable manually the form after adding a disabled control to an empty enabled form seems more a workaround than an expected working logic, to me...

Uh... @AndrewKushnir your stackblitz is wrong since you are enabling the form and all their children, while the issue I opened was about having the parent form enabled (and its' validator checked), while the children have to still be disabled.
